description: A team of six future electronic engineers combining expertise in hardware, electronics, communication systems, and data processing. We aim to develop viable, functional, and innovative solutions to the global challenges posed by NASA.
summary:
We developed SeMF (FIRMS Fire-Front Fusion), an end-to-end scientific and operational platform that unifies NASA FIRMS satellite data to monitor active wildfires and historical burning patterns.
To address the structural discontinuity between one-thousand-meter MODIS and three-hundred-seventy-five-meter VIIRS sensors, our three-phase physical harmonization engine computes true ground pixel footprints (scan multiplied by track) to normalize Fire Radiative Power Density in megawatts per square kilometer, cross-calibrates four-micrometer and eleven-micrometer infrared channels through their thermal differential to suppress false alarms, and maps disparate confidence scales onto a unified zero-to-one index without data loss. Using Geodesic DBSCAN clustering with the Haversine metric and a two-and-a-half-kilometer search radius, the system transforms isolated hotspots into consolidated fire fronts with affected area, spread speed, and cardinal heading.
Validated across the wildland-urban corridor of Córdoba and San Luis, Argentina, this platform is vital because it bridges orbital physics with frontline civil protection. It consolidates a bias-free twenty-six-year Historical Fire Calendar to detect seasonal anomalies while empowering everyday citizens, rural producers, and emergency responders with real-time web maps, open GIS exports, dynamic escape routing, and georeferenced SOS alerts.
details:
How It Works and Core Capabilities: SeMF (FIRMS Fire-Front Fusion) is an end-to-end scientific and operational platform that unifies near real-time (NRT) and historical satellite data from NASA FIRMS across MODIS (Terra and Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21) sensors. To overcome structural differences between 1000 m MODIS pixels and 375 m VIIRS pixels, our three-phase physical harmonization engine computes the true ground footprint of each pixel (scan multiplied by track) to normalize Fire Radiative Power Density in MW/km2, cross-calibrates the 4-micrometer and 11-micrometer infrared channels through their thermal differential (Delta T) to suppress false alarms, and projects disparate confidence metrics (0 to 100 percent versus low, nominal, and high flags) onto a continuous 0.0 to 1.0 scale without data loss. Next, a Geodesic DBSCAN clustering engine using the Haversine metric (Earth radius of 6371 km and search radius of 2.5 km) groups isolated hotspots into consolidated fire fronts, applying Convex Hull geometry and kinematic tracking to calculate affected area in hectares, spread speed in km/h, azimuth, and cardinal heading.

Benefits and Intended Impact: Designed primarily for everyday citizens, rural communities, and agricultural producers in wildland-urban interface zones, SeMF transforms raw orbital detections into actionable civil protection intelligence while remaining fully interoperable for firefighters and emergency agencies. Strategically, it delivers a bias-free 26-year Historical Fire Calendar (2000 to 2026) that eliminates artificial hotspot jumps caused by sensor evolution, enabling users to explore custom date ranges and geographic zones, identify seasonal burning baselines, and detect out-of-season anomalies. Operationally, it provides an interactive multi-layer web map, dynamic escape routing that guides citizens away from advancing fire vectors toward safe zones, georeferenced SOS distress alerts for low-connectivity rural areas, and open GIS exports (GeoJSON, CSV, and JSON) ready for QGIS and ArcGIS.

Tools, Coding Languages, and Software: The platform was developed in Python (3.10+) using pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, and SciPy for physical harmonization and geodesic clustering; Folium, Leaflet, HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript for the interactive web map and mobile-first tactical interface; and Matplotlib for statistical validation. The entire system is containerized with Docker and Docker Compose (app_server.py), includes automated unit tests, and relies exclusively on open NASA EOSDIS FIRMS NRT APIs and historical archives.

Creativity and Key Design Factors: Our creative approach bridges rigorous radiative transfer physics with human-centered emergency design, making complex multi-sensor orbital telemetry accessible on a smartphone during high-stress evacuations. Key engineering factors considered by our team included preventing data loss during multi-sensor merges, compensating for panoramic bow-tie pixel distortion across scan angles, enforcing physical plausibility filters (bounding revisit intervals, radiative density, and spread speeds between 0 and 35 km/h to eliminate sensor noise), protecting NASA API credentials on the backend, ensuring offline resilience with local data caching for rural areas with degraded 4G/5G coverage, and validating the entire system across the wildfire-prone Sierras de Córdoba and San Luis corridor in Argentina while keeping coordinates globally parameterizable.
